title: 16S rRNA Gene Library Preparation Protocol
author: dinesh.aggarwal
materials: UV the MPure machine before use.

Set Up the MPure 12 Reagents and plasticware: Place the reagent cartridge in the large flat block at the back, it should click into place, and the writing and release flap should be facing toward you. The clear plastic mixing wells are clipped in front of these. Then place the black plastic container set into the next slots, into the first of these place a plastic pin, in the third place a tip. Put an open labelled elution tube in the closest holes in the metal rack (labelled E).
Carefully remove the plate seal. Change gloves.
Wipe Down MSC and pipettes with DNAZap.
Briefly vortex and spin down the samples.

steps.title: Thaw and vortex samples
steps.instruction: Remove frozen samples, thaw in a 4 °C refrigerator, then vortex for 10 seconds.

steps.title: Transfer sample to Eppendorf tube
steps.instruction: Pipette‑mix and transfer up to 800 µL from the storage tube into a labelled 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Centrifuge sample
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube for 10 minutes at 13 200 rpm.

steps.title: Remove supernatant and resuspend pellet
steps.instruction: Discard 100 µL of supernatant, then resuspend the bacterial pellet in the remaining liquid.

steps.title: Transfer to lysis tube
steps.instruction: Transfer the resuspended volume to a labelled lysis tube containing Lysing Matrix E (MP Biomedicals) and label the side of the tube.

steps.title: Mechanical lysis
steps.instruction: Place lysis tubes in the FastPrep instrument and run for 40 seconds at speed 6000.

steps.title: Second centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysed tubes for 10 minutes at 13 500 rpm.

steps.title: Collect cleared lysate
steps.instruction: Transfer approximately 450 µL (or as close as possible) of supernatant from each lysis tube to a labelled blue sample tube from the MPure bacterial DNA extraction kit; place tubes in the metal rack slots “S”.

steps.title: Automated DNA extraction
steps.instruction: On the MPure extraction instrument, select protocol “MPure Bacterial DNA extraction kit” (barcode OP02006), set sample volume to 400 µL (barcode SV0400), elution volume to 50 µL (barcode EV0050), and start the run (~1 hour).

steps.title: Store eluted DNA
steps.instruction: Remove the elution tubes, verify a reasonable volume is present, and store them at –80 °C in a labelled box.

steps.title: Clean work area
steps.instruction: Wipe the MSC or PCR hood with DNAZap.

steps.title: Prepare primer working stocks
steps.instruction: Dilute each primer to a 10 mM working concentration in nuclease‑free water (stock is 100 mM) if no dilution younger than 2 weeks exists.

steps.title: Aliquot diluted primers
steps.instruction: Aliquot diluted primers into labelled linked PCR tubes; freeze upright overnight if necessary.

steps.title: Rack out library samples
steps.instruction: Place extracted DNA samples into a 12 × 8 rack according to the plate plan, add lid, label, and store at –80 °C. Include PCR negative controls, a positive mock community control, a PCR‑water negative control, and any diluted or spiked samples.

steps.title: Decontaminate MSC
steps.instruction: Wipe MSC with Distel/DNAZap, then 80 % ethanol; wipe all equipment with Distel, close MSC, and UV‑irradiate.

steps.title: Assemble master mix (water)
steps.instruction: Add 14.25 µL nuclease‑free water to each labelled master‑mix tube (one tube per well).

steps.title: Add Q5 buffer
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL Q5 buffer (from the Q5 High‑Fidelity Polymerase Kit, NEB) to each master‑mix tube and vortex/mix if salts have settled.

steps.title: Add dNTPs
steps.instruction: Add 0.5 µL of 10 mM dNTP mix to each master‑mix tube and vortex/mix.

steps.title: Keep master mix on ice
steps.instruction: Pipette‑mix the master mix and keep the tubes on ice.

steps.title: Record reagent lot numbers
steps.instruction: Document all reagent lot numbers on the library plate‑plan sheet; use the same PCR reagents for all samples when possible.

steps.title: Add Q5 enzyme
steps.instruction: Immediately before use, add 5 µL Q5 enzyme to each master‑mix tube, pipette‑mix, and keep on ice.

steps.title: Prepare PCR plate
steps.instruction: Label a 96‑well plate, add orientation marks, and place it on an ice block for the remainder of the setup.

steps.title: Dispense master mix
steps.instruction: Pipette 20 µL of master mix into each well of the 96‑well plate (no tip change required).

steps.title: Add primer set 501‑508
steps.instruction: Using a multichannel pipette in the vertical orientation, transfer 1.25 µL of each primer (501‑508) from the linked PCR tubes to the corresponding wells; change tips if the plate or tubes are touched and verify volume uptake.

steps.title: Add primer set 701‑712
steps.instruction: Using a multichannel pipette in the horizontal orientation, transfer 1.25 µL of each primer (701‑712) to the appropriate wells; change tips after each use and verify volume uptake.

steps.title: Seal plate and chill
steps.instruction: Apply a plate seal, move the sealed plate and its chiller unit into a second MSC if available.

steps.title: Retrieve DNA templates
steps.instruction: Retrieve the DNA‑template rack from the fridge, spray the closed rack into the MSC, and keep it on ice.

steps.title: Add DNA template
steps.instruction: Add 2.5 µL of each sample DNA template to the corresponding well (according to the plate plan); change tips for every addition and discard any tip that contacts other surfaces.

steps.title: Seal and press plate
steps.instruction: Apply a fresh plate seal, use a roller/squeegee to ensure proper sealing, and add autoclave tape around the edges if outer‑well loss is observed.

steps.title: Run PCR
steps.instruction: Place the plate in a PCR machine with heated lid and run: 98 °C 2 min; 32 cycles of 98 °C 30 s, 50 °C 30 s, 72 °C 1 min 30 s; final extension 72 °C 5 min; hold at 4 °C.

steps.title: Repeat PCR for triplicates
steps.instruction: Repeat steps 21–27 (primer addition, template addition, sealing, and PCR) until each library is prepared in triplicate.

steps.title: Freeze PCR plates
steps.instruction: Freeze the completed PCR plates at –20 °C before cleanup.

steps.title: Prepare AMPure beads
steps.instruction: Bring AMPure XP beads to room temperature, vortex the bead stock for 30 seconds, and pour into a trough.

steps.title: Combine triplicate PCR products
steps.instruction: Combine the three PCR replicates into a single 96‑well plate using a multichannel pipette.

steps.title: Add beads to PCR product
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of beads (≈75 µL) to each well of the combined PCR plate; pipette up/down 10 times, changing tips for each column.

steps.title: Incubate bead binding
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate at room temperature for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Magnetic separation – bind
steps.instruction: Place the plate on a magnetic stand for 2 minutes until the supernatant clears.

steps.title: Remove supernatant
steps.instruction: Using a multichannel pipette, remove and discard the supernatant (change tips each time); avoid disturbing the bead pellet.

steps.title: First ethanol wash
steps.instruction: While the plate remains on the magnetic stand, add 200 µL fresh 80 % ethanol to each well with a multichannel pipette.

steps.title: Second ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Add another 200 µL fresh 80 % ethanol to each well (still on the magnetic stand).

steps.title: Air‑dry beads
steps.instruction: Leave the plate on the magnetic stand for 10 minutes to air‑dry the beads.

steps.title: Elute DNA from beads
steps.instruction: Add 27.5 µL Tris‑HCl pH 8 to each well, pipette up/down 10 times to resuspend beads, then incubate at room temperature for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Second magnetic capture
steps.instruction: Place the plate back on the magnetic stand for 2 minutes (or until supernatant clears).

steps.title: Transfer eluate
steps.instruction: Using a multichannel pipette, transfer 25 µL from each well to a new labelled PCR plate; change tips between samples and avoid disturbing the bead pellet.

steps.title: Seal eluate plate
steps.instruction: Seal the new plate thoroughly; if freezing at –20 °C, wrap in aluminium foil and keep at 4 °C overnight.

steps.title: Prepare Qubit standards
steps.instruction: Label two Qubit tubes ‘S1’ and ‘S2’; add 10 µL Qubit HS Standard 1 to S1 and 10 µL Standard 2 to S2; keep on ice.

steps.title: Prepare Qubit working solution
steps.instruction: In a 50 mL Falcon tube, add 199 µL Qubit HS Buffer and 1 µL Qubit HS Reagent for each sample plus two standards; vortex briefly and protect from light.

steps.title: Prepare standard tubes
steps.instruction: Add 190 µL of the working solution to each standard tube, vortex 5 seconds, incubate 2 minutes, and ensure no bubbles.

steps.title: Calibrate Qubit
steps.instruction: Select the dsDNA HS assay on the Qubit fluorometer, calibrate using the two standard tubes, and record the standard values.

steps.title: Measure sample concentrations
steps.instruction: Vortex the remaining working solution, add 198 µL to each sample tube, add 2 µL of the DNA sample, vortex 5 seconds, incubate 2 minutes, then place the tube in the Qubit and record the concentration.

steps.title: Repeat Qubit measurements
steps.instruction: Repeat the previous step for all samples; dilute any sample with too high a concentration and repeat until a reliable value is obtained.

steps.title: Calculate equimolar volumes
steps.instruction: Identify the highest (e.g., 55.0 µg/mL) and lowest (e.g., 6.2 µg/mL) sample concentrations. For each sample, compute Volume (µL) = Desired DNA amount (µg) / Sample concentration (µg/mL). Use a maximum of 20 µL per sample and a minimum of 1 µL; if a sample’s concentration is <2 ng/µL, add the entire sample volume.

steps.title: Print volume list
steps.instruction: Print a 96‑well‑format list of the calculated volumes for each sample.

steps.title: Create equimolar pool
steps.instruction: In a labelled 2 mL screw‑cap tube, combine the calculated volumes of each PCR product (add the largest volumes first), pipette‑mix, and verify the total volume.

steps.title: Split equimolar pool
steps.instruction: Divide the pooled mixture in half; store one half at –20 °C in an O‑ring screw‑cap tube as a spare.

steps.title: Add loading dye
steps.instruction: Mix the unfrozen half of the equimolar pool with loading dye according to the dye’s instructions.

steps.title: Prepare agarose gel
steps.instruction: Make a 1 % agarose gel in 1× TBE with a nucleic‑acid stain of choice, cast it, and fill the buffer tank until the buffer level reaches the top of the gel.

steps.title: Run gel electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Run the gel for approximately 1 hour 30 minutes at 90 V (ensure the buffer level remains at the top of the gel).

steps.title: Visualize and excise bands
steps.instruction: Use a UV transilluminator to locate bands, cut them out with minimal excess gel, wear appropriate eye/face protection, and dispose of sharps properly.

steps.title: Weigh gel slices
steps.instruction: Weigh each 1.5 mL tube before and after adding a gel slice; record the weight of each gel slice.

steps.title: Add membrane binding solution
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL Membrane Binding Solution (Wizard SV Gel and PCR Clean‑Up Kit, Promega) per 10 mg of gel slice (e.g., for a 0.48 g slice add 480 µL), vortex briefly.

steps.title: Load gel onto minicolumn
steps.instruction: Place a Minicolumn into a collection tube, pipette up to 700 µL of dissolved gel into the column, and incubate 1 minute.

steps.title: Centrifuge minicolumn (first spin)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the Minicolumn at 13 200 rpm for 1 minute.

steps.title: Discard flow‑through
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant into a labelled liquid‑waste container and re‑insert the Minicolumn into the collection tube.

steps.title: Repeat gel loading
steps.instruction: Repeat the loading, centrifugation, and discard steps until no dissolved gel remains (i.e., until < 700 µL remains).

steps.title: First membrane wash
steps.instruction: Add 700 µL Membrane Wash Solution (add ethanol as instructed by the kit) to the column and centrifuge at 13 200 rpm for 1 minute.

steps.title: Second membrane wash
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL Membrane Wash Solution, centrifuge at 13 200 rpm for 5 minutes, then discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Final spin‑dry
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the column and collection tube at 13 200 rpm for 1 minute to remove residual wash solution.

steps.title: Elute DNA from column
steps.instruction: Transfer the Minicolumn to a 1.5 mL tube, add 100 µL nuclease‑free water directly onto the membrane, incubate 1 minute at room temperature, then centrifuge at 13 200 rpm for 1 minute.

steps.title: Check eluate completeness
steps.instruction: Verify that the water has passed through the membrane; if any liquid remains, repeat the previous elution step.

steps.title: Store final library
steps.instruction: Discard the Minicolumn, split the eluate into a labelled screw‑cap tube, keep half as a spare and submit the other half for sequencing.

steps.title: Add BLB2 buffer
steps.instruction: Add 600 µL BLB2 buffer (MPure Bacterial DNA Extraction Kit, MP Biomedicals) to the eluate and vortex to resuspend.

steps.title: Include extraction negative control
steps.instruction: Process a negative control (nuclease‑free water) for each kit batch (≈ every 50 samples) and record all associated metadata.

steps.title: Run gel for equimolar mix
steps.instruction: Run a 10‑minute, 90 V electrophoresis with buffer level at the top of the gel; the equimolar mix should migrate into the gel.

steps.title: Load equimolar mix
steps.instruction: Load the equimolar mix into the gel wells, filling each well as completely as possible.

steps.title: Dissolve gel slice
steps.instruction: Place the gel‑slice‑containing tube into a heat block at 55 °C until the gel fully dissolves; vortex intermittently to accelerate dissolution.

steps.title: Defrost and spin plates
steps.instruction: Defrost plates on ice, spin down before opening, and change gloves.

steps.title: Final magnetic clean‑up – ethanol removal
steps.instruction: Incubate the plate on the magnetic stand for 30 seconds, discard supernatant into waste, repeat for a second 30‑second incubation, then use a P20 with fine tips to remove any residual ethanol.

steps.title: Final MSC decontamination
steps.instruction: Clean the MSC with DNAZap.
